hook_text: Power lines carry enough electricity to kill. So why don't the pylons get electrified?
clip_script: A power line technician visits Ermelo. Rubber gloves, rubber boots, tools with plastic handles. All insulators! They stop electricity flowing through. Inside a plug: copper conducts, plastic insulates. On the pylon: bare metal wires, held up by glass discs, so electricity can't run down into the ground. But a cracked cord? Danger! Never tape it, never touch it. Get it fixed.
visual_style: Whiteboard pylon with glass discs, a cut plug showing copper inside plastic, and gloved hands holding an insulated screwdriver.
mood: Serious but empowering, like meeting a safety hero.
pacing: The gloves, the plug, the pylon, then the danger of damage.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the cords at home with an adult.
